core_obligations: Show that the second condition implies the first, by applying the characterisation of quasi-separated algebraic spaces to the reductions and using that the fibre products over the space and over its reduction agree (proof lines 3626-3631).
Assume the first condition, take two affine morphisms into the space, and observe that their fibre product is a scheme (proof lines 3633-3637).

Identify the reduction of the fibre product with the reduction of the fibre product of the reductions, conclude that it is affine with a surjective comparison map by the algebraic space characterisation, and hence that the fibre product is affine (proof lines 3639-3650).

Factor the comparison morphism to the product of the two affine schemes as a monomorphism locally of finite type followed by an immersion, and show it is integral by exhibiting a closed immersion on reduced affine schemes (proof lines 3650-3674).
Conclude that the induced ring map is an integral finite type epimorphism, hence finite and surjective (proof lines 3674-3683).
proof_roadmap: Fibre product is a scheme, and its reduction (proof lines 3633-3649).
Affineness of the fibre product (proof lines 3649-3650).
The comparison morphism and its properties (proof lines 3650-3674).
The ring map is a surjective finite epimorphism (proof lines 3674-3683).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states the equivalence of two conditions for a formal algebraic space: that its reduction is a separated algebraic space, and that for any two morphisms from affine schemes into the space the fibre product is affine and the natural map from the tensor product of the two coordinate rings to its coordinate ring is surjective (statement lines 3609-3624). One direction is short: the second condition applied to the reduction gives separatedness there, using the identification of the fibre products over the space and over its reduction (proof lines 3626-3631). The other direction is a genuine argument. Given the first condition and two affine morphisms, the fibre product is first seen to be a scheme; the reduction of the fibre product is identified with the reduction of the fibre product of the two reductions, which is affine with surjective comparison map by the corresponding characterisation for algebraic spaces, so the fibre product itself is affine (proof lines 3633-3650). Then the map from that fibre product to the product of the two affine schemes is factored as a monomorphism locally of finite type followed by an immersion, and shown to be integral because on reduced affine schemes it is a closed immersion; the induced ring map is therefore an integral finite type epimorphism, hence finite, hence surjective (proof lines 3650-3683). The claim is H3: after the short direction, the proof combines an identification of reductions, a criterion taking an algebraic space to an affine scheme, and a chain of properties of the comparison morphism ending in an algebra statement, so at least three independent mechanisms are used.
